explanation: No coherent trigger: fires on assorted subword fragments inside rare or technical words (al-ve-olar, sur-G-ical, W-olk-off, cardio-verter, a-ort-omesenteric) and on miscellaneous function words (some, shall, either, could, Let, A after 'A:'). The token identity and context do not share an obvious pattern.

Fires on the first subword piece of a word that is split into several tokens, especially word-initial fragments like 'contr' (contractions, contraindications, Contrary), 'nu', 'sur', 'ser', 'w', 'Mur', 'lymph'; strength depends on the token being an incomplete word-start whose continuation is predictable. Whole common words do not fire.

Fires on a determiner/quantifier or 'of' that opens a phrase expressing variety or number of kinds: 'there are [a] few/number', 'types [of]', 'three [different]/[separate]', 'some [other]', 'a [potential]'. Strongest on 'a' after 'there are' and on 'different/separate' after a number; plain articles elsewhere fire weakly.

Fires in programming Q&A / code-help contexts (StackOverflow-style questions, JavaScript/jQuery/AJAX code and comments) on tokens within the question text or code, often a determiner or technical noun ('with [a]', 'from [this]', 'your [AJAX]', '[nib]', '[jQuery]'). The technical-help context matters more than the specific token; prose outside such contexts fires weakly.

Fires on verbs of perception/regard used in the sense of 'being viewed/considered as' something: 'be [regarded] as', 'be [viewed] as', 'is [perceived]', 'be [seen] as/to', 'looked [upon]/[on]', '[treated] ... as', 'theory [views]'. Strongest when followed by an 'as'-complement framing; literal seeing ('can be seen removing') fires moderately.

No single trigger: fires on mid-word pieces in Russian/Turkish/Dutch words, on abbreviation pieces (e.g., 'e.g', 'yr', 'am', 'per'), and on assorted English words (agree, been, devoted, Probably, each). Examples look like a mixture of unrelated contexts.

Mixed: fires in legal opinions on words of the appellate holding formula ('did not err [in]', '[err]', 'affirm the [finding]', 'den[ials]', citation 'Rptr[.]'), and also in informal opinion/review prose on emphatic or evaluative tokens ('don['t]', 'you [must]', 'guys [really]', 'good [reviews]'), plus some code/hex tokens. No single concept unifies them.

Fires on the first subword fragment of a rare word or proper name that is split into pieces ('sup[ram]aximal', '[cur]tailed', '[Dec]atur', '[R]ana', '[fr]inges', 'Sch[öne]feld', 'ter[od]iline', 'St[oj]anović'), especially in scientific or legal text. Common whole words fire weakly.

Fires on the preposition (or article) that a preceding verb/noun selects, i.e. the governed preposition right after verbs like 'believe [in]', 'contrast/contrary/compared [to]', 'criticised/award/implications [for]', 'inspired [by]', 'indicate [a]', 'challenge/injection [of]'. Strongest for 'believe in' and 'in contrast to'; the preceding head word is what matters.

Fires on tokens expressing a minimum threshold requirement: 'at' in 'at least', and 'minimum' (minimum wage, minimum required version, a minimum of). Strongest for 'at' when 'least' follows in a requirement/specification context; weaker for related limit words (below, must, min).

Fires on a token that completes the subject noun phrase near the start of a news lede or abstract, before the main verb (e.g., 'A retired FBI agent [who]', 'A Florida [teenager]', 'An eight-year-old [boy]', 'The American novelist[,]', 'economic [and]'). Position early in a document/sentence opening matters more than the token identity; somewhat diffuse.

Fires mostly on words describing sports results and match structure ('losing', 'eliminated', 'beaten', 'loss', 'on [top]', '1st [set]', 'visit', batting '.[3]03'), and separately on network/hardware 'port(s)' in code or tech text, plus scattered other tokens. Two-plus unrelated jobs.

Fires in software license headers on specific boilerplate tokens: 'or' in 'version N of the License, or (at your option)', 'file' in 'LICENSE file', '.txt' in 'LICENSE.txt', and 'LICENSE'. Outside license boilerplate it fires only weakly on scattered tokens.

Fires on tokens inside license/legal boilerplate ('General Public [License]', 'binary [form]', '(the "[License]")', 'AS IS" [BASIS]', 'copyright [notice]', 'et [al]', counsel names), with some offshoot activations on random nouns in other formal text. Main job is legal/license boilerplate phrases.

Fires on words related to timekeeping and oscillation/timing devices (RTC Crystal, time synchronization, Watch, clock.h, pendulum, timezone, Date) and also on vestibular/balance and level-measurement terms (spirit level, vestibular). Strongest on clock/oscillator concepts.

Fires on the first token right after an opening parenthesis that begins a parenthetical aside, especially '(and', '(or', '(by', '(en', '(commonly', '(the', '(AP'. The open paren immediately before is the key context; the bare ' (' itself fires only moderately.

Fires in scientific/academic abstract prose at points of list continuation or citation/number insertion: a space before a number, a comma in a list of methods, citation brackets '\[@', and words like 'vs[.]' or 'followed [by]'. Mostly technical-paper context; token identity varies.

Fires in interview/press contexts on tokens marking who is speaking or being questioned: the colon after an interviewer label ('Wired.com[:]'), 'Q&[A]', 'responded to [questions]', 'told [reporters]', 'when [asked]', 'press [secretary]'. Context of media questions and answers is key.

Fires on the final subword piece of a place name (region, province, city, county), completing it: 'Sax[ony]', 'Pen[ang]', 'Brand[enburg]', 'Carmarthens[hire]', 'Fuku[oka]', 'Val[ais]', 'Wilt[shire]'. Whole-token place names fire weakly to moderately.

Fires on markup/syntax punctuation tokens that begin a command or tag: LaTeX backslash commands ('\usepackage', '^\infty', '{\'), HTML closing tags ('.</', '"></'), and doc-comment '@' annotations. Strongest at the start of a backslash or closing-tag token in code/math markup.

Mainly fires on the ' *' continuation line in C-style license/copyright comment blocks (especially after a blank ' *' line), and also on technical computing/patent nouns ('disk', 'shift register', 'plurality', 'security') and reference-numeral spaces in patents. Two loosely related technical-document jobs plus scattered tokens.
